pending_tags.title: Great Toad Sage of Mount Myoboku

Rendered "el Sabio Sapo del Monte Myoboku" / "el Sabio Montaña Sapo". "Monte Myoboku" itself is confirmed by the Planeta character guide (recurring as "monte Myóboku"); the "Great Toad Sage" title is Jiraiya's own comedic exaggeration in-universe (not the same as "Ogama Sennin", the actual toad elder character named later in the guide) and has no direct official rendering. The place name is confirmed; only the title "Sabio Sapo" is pending. Re-checked 2026-09-24: guide vol.3 p.84 confirms "Ogama Sennin" as the distinct real toad-elder name, matching this entry's own reasoning; still no hit for a "Gran Sabio Sapo" title itself.

No source found in the manga/guide database; literal translation of the English fansub terms (the seal's canonical Japanese name is Hakke no Fūin Shiki). Checked 2026-09-24: no hit for "trigrama(s)" anywhere in the OCR database — Planeta consistently keeps "hakke" as an untranslated loanword instead (e.g. "Hakke rokujúyon shó", "Hakke kú shó"; see the now-resolved 64PALMAS = "64 signos hakke"). Suggests "Ocho Trigramas" may not be how Spain renders "hakke" here either, but no direct hit for this specific seal concept (distinct from Neji's techniques), so left pending rather than guessed.

pending_tags.title: Chūnin/Jōnin macron inconsistency
pending_tags.body: The glossary's verified:false entry for "Chūnin"/"Jōnin" keeps the macron, and S01E01/S01E03 used it that way, but S01E09 (Christian-reviewed, 2026-09-22) dropped the macron to "Chunin"/"Jonin" throughout. S01E10 continues directly from S01E09's arc, so it follows S01E09's no-macron spelling for consistency with the immediately preceding episode, diverging from the glossary and from S01E01/S01E03. Only the first occurrence in S01E10 is tagged (cue 102); the word is too frequent to tag every instance. Needs a decision on which spelling is canonical, then a pass to unify S01E01/S01E03 (or S01E09/S01E10) to match. Checked 2026-09-24: Planeta doesn't use "Chunin"/"Jonin" as loanwords at all — it translates the rank as "grado medio" throughout (e.g. Naruto vol.4 pp.140-164). Interesting, but doesn't settle the macron question on its own since the loanword itself isn't used in the source.
